channel.title: Quiet Days Books
channel.description: Small books for noticing the animal you live with, while they are here.

item.title: What Do Cats See? Colour, Dark and Detail Explained
item.description: Cats most likely have two kinds of colour cells, like red-green colour blindness. They see far better in dim light and catch small movements, but lose detail.

item.title: How Long Do Dachshunds Live? Standard vs Miniature
item.description: Dachshunds live about 13 to 14 years. A 2024 UK study found a median of 13.2 for standard Dachshunds and 14.0 for miniatures, among the longest of 155 breeds.

item.title: How Long Do Yorkies Live? What the Studies Show
item.description: Yorkies live about 13 to 14 years. UK vet records give a median age at death of 13.56, and a 2024 study of 14,579 Yorkshire Terriers found 13.3 years.

item.title: How Long Do Indoor Cats Live? What Studies Measured
item.description: Indoor cats often live into their teens: pet cats average 12 to 14 years, and late teens or early twenties are not unusual. No study has timed indoor-only cats.

item.title: Why Do Cats Meow at Night? Reasons and What Helps
item.description: Cats meow at night because their active hours peak around dusk and dawn, and because meowing is how they ask people for food or attention. What helps.

item.title: How Long Do French Bulldogs Live? Three UK Studies
item.description: French Bulldogs live a median of 9.8 years in a 2024 study of 11,821 UK Frenchies. Why vet-record studies said 3.6 and 4.5 years, and what that means.

item.title: How Long Do Labs Live? What UK Data Shows
item.description: Labs live about 12 to 13 years. A 2024 study of 43,428 UK Labradors found a median of 13.1; vet records give 12.0, and chocolate Labs lived less.

item.title: Cat Body Language: Ears, Eyes, Tail and Posture
item.description: Cat body language: forward ears, slow blinks and an upright tail mean relaxed; flat ears, wide pupils and a low, tight body mean worried. Chart and research.

item.title: Can Dogs Eat Parsnips? Plain, Boiled and in Moderation
item.description: Yes, plain boiled parsnip is on PDSA's dog-safe Christmas list. Skip honey glaze, oil, butter and seasoning, and keep dogs away from wild parsnip plants.

item.title: Can Dogs Eat Candy Canes? Xylitol, Wrappers, Shards
item.description: No. Candy canes are sugar and peppermint, sugar-free ones may hold xylitol, which is toxic to dogs, and wrappers can block the gut. What to do if yours ate one.

item.title: Do Dogs Get Cold? Signs, Temperatures and Coats
item.description: Yes, dogs get cold. Most are fine above 45°F (7°C); below 32°F (0°C) small, thin-coated, old or ill dogs are at risk. Signs to watch and when a coat helps.

item.title: Can Dogs Eat Sweet Potatoes? Cooked, Plain, Small
item.description: Yes, if the sweet potato is cooked, peeled and plain, in small amounts. Raw pieces, casserole with marshmallows and seasoned fries are the ones to skip.

item.title: How Cold Is Too Cold for Cats? Indoors and Outside
item.description: Cats Protection says below about 7°C (45°F) can start to be unsafe for a cat outside. Indoors, cats find warm spots. Here is how to tell if yours is cold.

item.title: Can Dogs Eat Cranberry Sauce? Sugar, Raisins, Alcohol
item.description: A taste of plain cranberry sauce is probably safe, but it is high in sugar, and sauces with raisins, brandy or xylitol are not. Plain cranberries are safer.

item.title: Christmas Cat Names, Grouped, Plus Nicknames That Stick
item.description: Christmas cat names grouped by coat colour, personality, food, films and other languages, plus December nicknames for the cat you already live with.

item.title: Can Dogs Eat Gravy? Onion, Salt and Fat Explained
item.description: Not the gravy on your table: it often has onion or garlic, salty stock cubes and fat. A drizzle you know is free of those is a different matter; ask your vet.

item.title: Dog Name Generator: Names From What You Can See
item.description: A dog name generator that starts from your dog's coat, size, the way they move or the sounds they make. Draw a few names or read the whole list.

item.title: Can Dogs Eat Stuffing? Why It Stays on Your Plate
item.description: No, dogs shouldn't eat stuffing: most recipes use onion and garlic, which damage a dog's red blood cells, plus butter, salt and add-ins like raisins or nuts.

item.title: Can Dogs Eat Pumpkin Pie? What's Risky in a Slice
item.description: No, keep pumpkin pie for people: the filling is sugar, fat, dairy and spice, and sugar-free pies may hold xylitol. Plain 100% pumpkin is the dog-safe swap.

item.title: How Long Do Chihuahuas Live? What the Data Shows
item.description: Chihuahuas live a median of 11.8 years in a 2024 study of 584,734 UK dogs, and some pass 20. Why other figures look lower, and what the spread means.

item.title: Fun Facts About Cats: 29 Checked, With Sources
item.description: 29 fun facts about cats, each checked: they hear three times higher than us, can't taste sugar, have 24 whiskers, lap four times a second and know their names.

item.title: Cat Name Generator: Names From What You Can See
item.description: A cat name generator that starts from your cat's coat, the way they move or the sounds they make. Draw a few names at a time or read the whole list.

item.title: How Long Do German Shepherds Live? UK Data by Sex
item.description: German Shepherds live about 10 to 11 years. UK vet records give a median of 10.3, with females at 11.1 and males at 9.7; a 2024 study of 19,908 found 11.3.

item.title: Do Cats Dream? What Sleep Science Can and Can't Say
item.description: Cats almost certainly dream: they have REM sleep, and in Jouvet's studies sleeping cats stalked, pounced and groomed. What they dream about, nobody can know.

item.title: Why Does My Cat Stare at Me? What the Look Means
item.description: Cats stare to watch you, read your face or ask for something. Soft eyes and slow blinks are friendly; a hard, unblinking stare with wide pupils means back off.

item.title: How Long Do Golden Retrievers Live? What Data Shows
item.description: Golden Retrievers live about 13 years. A 2024 study of 11,506 UK Goldens found a median of 13.2 years, longer than the 11.9 average for large breeds.

item.title: Why Do Dogs Sleep So Much? Hours by Age, and Why
item.description: Dogs sleep about 10 hours a day on average, in short cycles, mostly at night with an afternoon rest. Older dogs nap more by day. What studies show.

item.title: Cat Keepsake Ideas From the Life You Share Now
item.description: Cat keepsake ideas from everyday life: a whisker that fell out on its own, fur from the brush, a retired collar, the box they claimed, a few seconds of sound.

item.title: Why Does My Cat Bring Me Toys? Play, Hunting, You
item.description: Cats bring you toys to finish a hunt somewhere safe and, often, to start a game. Many learn to fetch untaught and decide themselves when play starts and ends.

item.title: How Much Should You Walk a Senior Dog? A Gentle Guide
item.description: Walk a senior dog little and often: shorter routes, more stops, cooler hours, every day. How long depends on the dog, so watch how they cope and ask your vet.
